summary: Iteration 58 tested new PATCH & DELETE /api/leads/{id}/followups/{fid} endpoints + auto-slot override UI + FollowUpEditDialog. All 15 backend tests passed (creator/admin edit+delete, staff 403, 404 unknown, 400 empty payload, next_follow_up move on latest, unchanged on older, edited_by fields set, assignee notification on reschedule, regressions for POST followup + next-followup-slot). Frontend end-to-end verified: (1) as staff with 2 booked follow-ups, opening a 3rd follow-up lead shows data-testid='followup-auto-slot' with the auto slot value + 'Change' button; clicking Change swaps to datetime input with 'Use auto-slot' revert, which restores the auto-slot pill. (2) LeadJourney edit chip data-testid='followup-edit-<id>' visible, opens dialog data-testid='followup-edit-dialog' with datetime input pre-filled, note textarea, save + delete buttons. Save with +2h → 'Follow-up updated' toast → journey refreshes. Delete → confirm → 'Follow-up deleted' toast → chip removed. All seeded test leads cleaned up via DELETE /api/leads/{id}.
critical_code_review_comments: delete_followup uses remaining[-1]['at'] to recompute next_follow_up. This assumes follow_ups is stored in chronological order, which is true if only appended. If any historical data ever inserts out-of-order (bulk import etc), the surface value could regress. Consider `max(r['at'] for r in remaining)` for defence in depth.

update_followup compares old_at == lead.next_follow_up to detect 'this is the latest one'. If two follow-ups happen to share the same `at` (rare but not enforced unique), editing an OLDER one that coincidentally equals next_follow_up would move next_follow_up incorrectly. Minor; unlikely in practice.
FollowUpEditDialog `toIso` uses `new Date(localValue).toISOString()` — correct, though a millisecond fractional part is included in the persisted ISO. Backend stores as-is; harmless.
